defects.title: The shipped USDA food items file is not found
defects.observed: error 'Could not find USDA2024_foodItems.mat in <toolbox>/papers/2025_nutritionToolbox/usdaDatabase or on the MATLAB path.'; the shipped file (also on papers origin/master) is USDAFoodItems.mat
defects.expected: the path of the shipped USDA food items file (help text lists 'foodItems' (usda))

notes: LEAD DECISION: the 'usda'/'foodItems' failure is recorded as limitation (quarantine false) because the function builds the name createUSDAdatabase writes (USDA<YEAR>_foodItems.mat) and the mismatch is the shipped data file name USDAFoodItems.mat in papers/2025_nutritionToolbox/usdaDatabase (same on the papers submodule's origin/master). If the lead classes it as an error/unusable-option of getNutritionDatabaseFile instead, the callers using that call form are vmhFoodFinder (line 106) and nutritionAlgorithmWBM (line 628). Repro: getNutritionDatabaseFile('usda','foodItems') -> error above. The test does not assert anything about 'foodItems'. Default-edition sections compare with an independent listing of the papers folders (frida2024 and USDA2024 shipped, no blsDatabase folder -> the 'No bls database' error); if the submodule is not checked out, lines 79-80 would not be reached on that machine. On-path lookup tested with fictitious edition 1999 files in a tempname folder (path restored).

defects.title: needsLinux makes every test skip on Linux
defects.observed: error COBRA:RequirementsNotMet 'This test only works on Linux Systems' although isunix = 1; computer('arch') = 'glnxa64', line 177 compares with 'glnx64'

notes: Lead note confirmed. Repro: prepareTest('needsLinux', true) -> COBRA:RequirementsNotMet 'This test only works on Linux Systems' (probe: isunix=1 arch=glnxa64). The defect is confined to the call form 'needsLinux', true; no src caller passes it (createTissueSpecificModel, findFluxConsistentSubset do not). The quarantine test still calls prepareTest() in its standard opening (every test does), so some lines are hit; all lines are listed as exempt.
confirmed_by: lead (source read: needsLinux compares computer('arch') with 'glnx64'; Linux returns 'glnxa64', line 177)

defects.title: MATLAB_too = true always raises an error
defects.trigger: d = tempname; mkdir(d); sp = py.sys.path; sp.insert(int64(0), d); py_rmpath(d, true)
defects.observed: error "Undefined function 'rnpath' for input arguments of type 'char'." on line 48 (misspelling of rmpath); the folder was already removed from sys.path
defects.expected: folder removed from sys.path and the MATLAB path

notes: Repro: d = tempname; mkdir(d); sp = py.sys.path; sp.insert(int64(0), d); py_rmpath(d, true) -> Undefined function 'rnpath' (line 48). Confined to the call form with a true second argument; the only caller initPythonEnvironment calls py_rmpath(x, 0) (lines 143, 171, 192), so it does not reach the defect. Probe also showed: a relative folder is converted to absolute and removed correctly; py_rmpath('') returns sys.path unchanged (unlike py_addpath).
confirmed_by: lead (source read: line 48 calls rnpath, a misspelling of rmpath, when MATLAB_too is true)

defects.title: Python path entries with blanks are reported as differences
defects.trigger: setenv('PYTHONPATH', fullfile(d, 'a b')) before MATLAB's Python starts, then comparePaths('PYTHON')
defects.observed: system_not_matlab = {'<d>/ab'}, matlab_not_system = {'<d>/a b', ...}: line 39 deletes every blank of the system entries; entries with commas or quotes are also split

notes: Requires 'python' (system, called by line 31) and 'python3' (MATLAB pyenv), declared with requiredSoftwares. Uses its own environment variables (removed with unsetenv at the end); the two-blank entry '/opt/b  c' makes the two sides differ because echo $NAME is unquoted. PYTHON section compared with sys.path read independently from system python and py.sys.path; the test asserts no entry has blanks/commas/quotes so the limitation is skipped. Out-of-process Python is terminated if the test started it.

defects.observed: 'C2Cl3H2', protons = 2 (line 50 sorts new elements with setdiff, line 55 adds coefficients in formula order)

defects.title: A formula that loses all its hydrogen atoms keeps one H
defects.observed: 'HO4S', protons = 0 (phosphate 'HO4P', carbonate 'CHO3'): H0 written, then 'H0' replaced by 'H'

notes: Repro: [f,p] = getFormulaFromInChI('InChI=1S/C2H3Cl/c1-2-3/h2H,1H2/p+1') -> 'C2Cl3H2', 2; [f,p] = getFormulaFromInChI('InChI=1S/H2O4S/c1-5(2,3)4/h(H2,1,2,3,4)/p-2') -> 'HO4S', 0; also 'InChI=1S/2ClH.Co/h2*1H;/q;;+2/p-2' -> 'Cl2HCo', 0 (expected Cl2Co). Correct for pyruvate (/p-1 -> C3H3O3, 3), water, hydroxide and non-/p InChIs without composite parts (those take the else branch, line 68). Both defects are on the combining path (lines 34-64: /p layer, composite '.' or leading multiplier), which every call can reach depending on the InChI, so all callers reach it (getFormulaAndChargeFromInChI, modelMetabolitesToSDF, regulariseModelFormulae). Note also the combining path reorders elements alphabetically (setdiff), unlike the else branch.
confirmed_by: lead (writer's MATLAB reproductions: element counts assigned to the wrong elements for C2H3Cl, and a proton added to sulfate with /p-2)
